description: Master Catalog of Cloud Server Failure Scenarios, Edge Cases, and Performance Bottlenecks for FerroOS Testing and Resilience Evaluation.
workflow_policy: Strict Analysis-First Protocol: All discovered scenarios are marked [QUEUED_FOR_ANALYSIS]. No OS kernel or userspace code modifications may be made until the scenario is empirically analyzed.

scenarios.title: Relational OLTP Database Server (TPC-B Banking Transactions)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: High-frequency ACID transactions contending on shared write-ahead logs (WAL) and memory-mapped files under concurrent connections.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Lock contention on WAL index, fsync wait stalls, memory churn during commit surges.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: mimalloc 2.1 thread-local arenas prevent heap contention; libferro_io accelerates synchronous WAL flushes.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; bounded transaction pooling.

scenarios.title: Mail MTA & Spool Server (VFS Inode / Dentry Churn)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Rapid creation, atomic rename, and unlinking of millions of micro-files in Maildir directories causing severe dentry cache pressure.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: VFS lookup degradation, dcache lock serialization, ext4/xfs inode table exhaustion.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Lightweight memory-backed dentries and tmpfs spooling isolate disk I/O from critical path.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Tune vfs_cache_pressure to 50; batched unlinks.

scenarios.title: In-Memory Cache BGSAVE Fork & Copy-on-Write Latency Spike
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Background snapshotting via fork() duplicates page tables, causing latency spikes for write operations due to page fault Copy-On-Write overhead.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: p99 latency spikes exceeding 100ms on write commands during RDB saves; potential OOM under 50% memory headroom.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Sub-millisecond page table cloning in ferro-core avoids fork freeze; mimalloc transparent hugepage tuning mitigates TLB misses.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Disable transparent hugepages for Redis process; enable incremental AOF with fsync everysec.

scenarios.title: Nginx + Python Reverse Proxy & TLS 1.3 REST API Concurrency
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: High-volume HTTPS requests requiring ephemeral session resumption, JSON parsing, and upstream connection keep-alive management.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: CPU saturation on TLS handshakes, upstream socket pool exhaustion, 502 Bad Gateway errors.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: libferro_io non-blocking socket dispatch and hardware AES/ChaCha acceleration sustain line-rate throughput.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: TLS session ticket caching; SO_REUSEPORT multi-worker socket sharding.

scenarios.title: MinIO / Cloud Object Storage S3 Streaming & Hash Validation
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Concurrent multi-part 64MB blob streaming with inline SHA-256 and MD5 checksum computation.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Page cache dirty page buildup, disk I/O writeback stalls, memory thrashing under burst writes.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Zero-copy splice() / sendfile() bypasses userspace memory copy; SIMD SHA-256 pipeline minimizes CPU cycles.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Direct I/O (O_DIRECT) for blobs > 16MB to bypass page cache dirtying.

scenarios.title: NATS / Kafka Event Streaming & Log Ingestion Pipeline
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Ultra-high-throughput message ingestion requiring atomic queue updates and low-latency futex wakeups.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Futex lock convoying, CPU context-switch storm, buffer overflow drops under consumer lag.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Lock-free circular ring buffers and epoll event batching eliminate kernel transitions.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Batch event writes; tune socket SO_RCVBUF to 4MB.

scenarios.title: Search Engine & Log Analytics Server (FTS5 / BM25 Inverted Index)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Concurrent read queries performing inverted index scans against 100k+ documents with concurrent document indexing.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: High memory consumption on posting lists, disk seek latency on unbuffered index segments.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Fast memory-mapped index pages and vector instruction tokenization maintain sub-10ms queries.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Optimize SQLite FTS5 prefix and trigram tokenizers.

scenarios.title: Git & CI/CD Build Runner (Process Storm & Subshell Forking)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Rapid creation and destruction of hundreds of short-lived compiler, make, and shell processes.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: PID allocation lock contention, fork/exec page table copy overhead, process table exhaustion.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: ferro-init's sub-millisecond process reaper and posix_spawn() acceleration keep fork overhead < 1ms.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Use posix_spawn instead of fork+exec; increase /proc/sys/kernel/pid_max to 4194304.

scenarios.title: FFmpeg & Media Transcoding Worker (Multi-threaded SIMD Churn)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Compute-bound image/video filtering with heavy NEON/AVX2 vector instructions and large frame buffer allocations.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: CPU core thermal throttling, memory allocator fragmentation from variable-sized frame buffers.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: mimalloc 2.1 thread-local arenas isolate large buffer reallocations from small thread metadata.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Thread pool pinned to physical core boundaries without oversubscribing.

scenarios.title: Vector Database & AI Embedding Server (HNSW Cosine Similarity)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Approximate nearest neighbor graph traversal across high-dimensional vector spaces in RAM.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Random memory access latency, CPU L3 cache thrashing, p99 search latency degradation under load.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Compact struct layout and SIMD dot-product routines maximize CPU cache hit rates.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Aligned 64-byte vector memory boundaries for direct cacheline loading.

scenarios.title: Time-Series Telemetry & Metric Ingestion (High-Cardinality TSDB)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Millions of timestamped data points with unique label combinations streaming into an append-only time-series store.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Index bloat, high compression CPU overhead (Gorilla / Zstd), disk write amplification.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Chunked streaming compression with zlib/zstd in userspace buffers keeps disk writes batched and sequential.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Batch metric flushes every 250ms; tune double-delta timestamp compression.

scenarios.title: Multi-Tenant Hyper-Density Chaos Test (5 Concurrent Micro-Services)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Multiple independent application services (DB, cache, API, worker, metrics) running simultaneously in a shared 4–6 GB RAM envelope.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Resource starvation, CFS cpu-shares fight, noisy-neighbor memory pressure triggering unexpected OOM.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: ferro-core cgroup isolation and lightweight kernel memory footprint preserve headroom for all tenants.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Cgroup v2 memory.high soft throttling with memory.max hard limits.

scenarios.title: The $12 Cloud Droplet Concurrency Choke (1 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 0 Swap)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Extreme concurrency (500–10,000 VUs) on an entry-level cloud instance ($12/mo) running SQLite WAL social feed API.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Head-of-line socket queue blocking under unthrottled load; physical core saturation at 500 VUs.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: FerroOS's sub-30 MB idle footprint and mimalloc 2.1 thread-local arenas natively satisfy the challenge (10k VUs at 337 µs median) with zero OS kernel changes.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Zero OS Code Modifications Needed (Architectural Invariance Verified). Bounded userspace queue (32 in-flight) for unthrottled bursts.

scenarios.title: Ephemeral Port Exhaustion & TIME_WAIT Socket Saturation
scenarios.source: Cloud Outage Pattern (RFC 793 / AWS NAT & Outbound Proxy)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Microservices opening short-lived outbound TCP connections to databases or APIs exhaust the local ephemeral port range (ip_local_port_range, ~28,000 ports) due to sockets lingering in TIME_WAIT for 60 seconds.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Cannot assign requested address (EADDRNOTAVAIL); outbound API requests stall completely; services fail health checks.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: FerroOS socket recycling and SO_REUSEPORT connection pooling can reclaim closed TCP control blocks in < 100 µs.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Enable net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse = 1 and expand ip_local_port_range = 10240 65535.

scenarios.title: Linux Dirty Page Writeback Freeze (Flusher Stall)
scenarios.source: Linux Kernel Flusher Bug (vm.dirty_ratio Cloud Burst Issue)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Rapid sequential disk writes fill the Linux page cache up to vm.dirty_ratio (typically 20% of RAM). When the threshold is reached, all subsequent write() syscalls synchronously block while kernel flusher threads flush dirty pages to slow cloud block storage.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Entire application freezes for 2–15 seconds; p99 latency spikes into seconds; cloud watchdog kills the process.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: libferro_io async ring I/O with direct I/O (O_DIRECT) bypasses the page cache dirty threshold entirely.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Tune vm.dirty_background_ratio = 5 and vm.dirty_ratio = 10 to smooth out writeback bursts.

scenarios.title: CFS Bandwidth Quota Micro-Throttling (Kubernetes / Cgroups)
scenarios.source: Cloud Native Incident (Container CPU Throttling Outage)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Even when overall CPU utilization is below 50%, bursty multi-threaded applications exhaust their CFS quota (cpu.cfs_quota_us) early in the 100ms period, causing the Linux scheduler to freeze all threads until the next period begins.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Unexpected 100ms latency spikes on API responses despite low average CPU usage; 504 Gateway Timeouts.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: FerroOS sched_ext balanced quantum (2,000–5,000 µs) prevents premature quota exhaustion on single-core containers.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Tune cpu.cfs_period_us to 10,000 µs (10ms) or remove artificial CPU quotas on single vCPU instances.

scenarios.title: Thundering Herd Cache Stampede (Dogpiling on Redis Key Expiry)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: When a hot cached key expires under 10,000 concurrent requests, all incoming requests simultaneously miss the cache and issue redundant heavy queries to the backend database.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Database CPU spikes to 100%; connection pool exhaustion; cascading database crash across all web nodes.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: In-process lock-free single-flight mutex pattern or XFetch probabilistic early expiration in FerroOS middleware shields the database.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Implement singleflight promise coalescing in userspace; jittered TTLs.

scenarios.title: TCP SYN Backlog Saturation under Ingress Micro-Bursts
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Sudden arrival of hundreds of TCP handshakes in a few milliseconds overflows the kernel TCP listen backlog (tcp_max_syn_backlog and somaxconn), causing the kernel to drop incoming SYN packets without sending RST.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Clients experience 1-second or 3-second TCP SYN retransmission delays; connection setup appears hung.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Zero-drop lock-free SYN cookies and multi-queue SO_REUSEPORT sharding in FerroOS sustain 100,000+ handshakes/sec.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Set net.core.somaxconn = 65535 and net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog = 65535.

scenarios.title: Linux OOM Killer Priority Inversion (Critical Database Killed)
scenarios.source: Production Cloud Post-Mortem (Database OOM Kill Incident)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: A rogue worker script leaks memory, but because the primary database process (PostgreSQL / SQLite / MySQL) holds more RSS, the Linux kernel calculates a higher oom_score for the database and terminates the database instead of the rogue process.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Catastrophic database termination; data corruption during uncommitted transactions; extended downtime.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: ferro-init's proactive cgroup memory accounting isolates runaway workers before global kernel OOM fires.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Set /proc/$PID/oom_score_adj = -1000 for database daemon; set strict memory.max on worker cgroups.

scenarios.title: epoll Edge-Triggered Socket Event Starvation (Head-of-Line)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: In an EPOLLET event loop, a busy connection streaming megabytes of data keeps reading in a loop until EAGAIN, starving hundreds of other pending client connections on the same event loop.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Sub-millisecond p50 latency but extreme p99 tail latency blowouts (> 2,000ms); client connection timeouts.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Bounded event dispatch quantum with fair cooperative round-robin scheduling in libferro_io prevents loop monopolization.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Enforce maximum byte/packet read budget per socket per epoll_wait cycle (e.g., 64 KB).

scenarios.title: SQLite WAL Checkpoint Lock Stall on Continuous Reader Workload
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: When active read queries continuously hold read locks on older WAL snapshots, SQLite passive checkpointing (wal_checkpoint) cannot advance. The WAL file grows unbounded to multiple gigabytes, causing queries to scan huge WAL files.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Read query latency degrades 10x to 100x; disk space exhaustion; final forced checkpoint freezes the database.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: FerroOS transaction time-slicing and bounded concurrency prevent overlapping read lock cascades.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Run periodic PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) on dedicated maintenance connection; bound reader transaction lifespans.

scenarios.title: File Descriptor Exhaustion (EMFILE Cascading Service Collapse)
scenarios.source: Unix Cloud Server Limit Breach (Too many open files)
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: An application leaks socket or file handles under connection surges. Once the process hits its ulimit -n limit, subsequent accept() or open() calls fail with EMFILE.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: accept() returns EMFILE; epoll immediately re-triggers (CPU spins at 100%); service completely freezes.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Pre-allocated reserve file descriptor pattern in FerroOS allows graceful socket closure and immediate rejection.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Increase nofile ulimit to 1048576; implement reserve dummy FD trick to cleanly close over-limit connections.

scenarios.title: TCP Zero-Window Probe Deadlock under Slow Consumer Attack
scenarios.cloud_problem_description: Malicious or slow clients advertise a TCP Receive Window of 0 bytes. The server buffers responses in kernel socket buffers (SO_SNDBUF) and repeatedly sends zero-window probes without closing the connection.
scenarios.symptoms_and_impact: Kernel socket buffer memory exhaustion; thousands of idle connections tie up worker threads.
scenarios.ferro_os_hypothesis: Zero-window timeout enforcement and zero-copy user-space buffer caps drop uncooperative consumers in < 5s.
scenarios.minimal_elevation_knob: Configure tcp_retries2 = 5 and enforce application-level response write timeouts.
